prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S091: Ambulance Coordination Platform uses the recorded priority alongside unit availability and operational constraints when coordinating response resources.
S092: Radio Coordinator communicates dispatch instructions and priority changes over Regional Radio Network.
S093: Paramedic Crew reports material changes in patient condition so that the incident can be reassessed promptly.
S094: Ambulance Unit 417 follows the active dispatch instructions and requests clarification when the incident details do not support safe response.
S095: Emergency Department may provide operationally relevant capacity information, while clinical triage remains governed by approved regional protocols.
S096: Riverside Trauma Center is considered for destination coordination when the patient's needs and current clinical guidance support that option.
S097: Shift Commander is notified when competing high-priority incidents exceed available response capacity or require an operational exception.
S098: Data Quality Officer reviews whether priority changes and their supporting rationale are recorded consistently for later assessment.
S099: Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S100: Triage Supervisor reviews significant disagreements about urgency and records the basis for the final operational priority.
S101: Resource selection begins after the operational priority and essential response requirements have been confirmed.
S102: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents units whose reported status and capabilities match the incident requirements.
S103: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays estimated travel times, unit availability, and relevant access constraints.
S104: The Triage Supervisor confirms that the selected response level remains consistent with the caller information.
S105: The selection decision weighs clinical need, travel time, vehicle capability, crew readiness, and regional coverage.
S106: The Fleet Maintenance Cell provides current information about vehicles that are unavailable or restricted.
S107: The Radio Coordinator checks that the proposed unit can be reached on the Regional Radio Network.
S108: A dispatcher may recommend a unit, but dispatch authorization must follow the current regional approval rules.
S109: The Shift Commander approves exceptions that would materially reduce local coverage or require a nonstandard response.
S110: The Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical resource requirements when the incident presents an unusual care need.
S111: The dispatcher records the authorized unit and any conditions attached to its assignment.
S112: Regional Dispatch Center produces the Unit Staging Change Card when a previously selected unit must be repositioned.
S113: The Radio Coordinator selects the appropriate talkgroup and confirms that it is available before transmitting.
S114: The dispatch transmission states the incident identifier, location, priority, response assignment, and any immediate hazard information.
S115: The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the assignment and repeats the location and priority for confirmation.
S116: The dispatcher corrects any discrepancy through a fresh transmission rather than relying on an unclear acknowledgment.
S117: If the assigned unit does not acknowledge promptly, the Radio Coordinator attempts contact again and alerts the dispatch supervisor.
S118: The North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board support routing decisions when access conditions are changing.
S119: Dispatchers state a confirmed gate or approach constraint explicitly and identify any uncertainty in the information.
S120: The controlled handoff occurs when the crew has acknowledged the assignment and the dispatch floor has confirmed the essential details.
S121: The Paramedic Crew reports any material conflict between the transmitted route and conditions observed in the field.
S122: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination information with the receiving Emergency Department when required.
S123: Radio Coordinator sends the Coverage Gap Bulletin when available ambulance coverage falls below the regional threshold.
S124: Juniper records the authorization time and the reason for selecting the assigned unit.
S125: Regional Dispatch Center maintains a regional coverage picture from current unit locations, crew reports, and readiness information.
S126: Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates unit position and status so dispatchers can compare available coverage across the region.
S127: Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents staging options that account for response demand, travel time, and access constraints.
S128: Paramedic Crew reports when a unit is available, responding, on scene, transporting, or temporarily unavailable.
S129: Crews update their status promptly after a material change so dispatch decisions reflect the unit's actual condition.
S130: Regional Radio Network carries route instructions and crew acknowledgments between dispatch and field units.
S131: Mistral confirms approved route changes over the Regional Radio Network before a crew diverts.
S132: Bluejay verifies maintenance clearance before a unit returns to available status.
S133: Ambulance Unit 417 reports its position and operating status when it enters or leaves a staging area.
S134: A crew remains at its assigned staging point until dispatch confirms a new location or a direct response assignment.
S135: South Gate Status Board displays current access conditions for units approaching the southern entry.
S136: Sundial reviews the regional coverage picture before approving a staging move.
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
